shortcut_name: product forces every edge sum to 3
evidence: "Color the graph with BFS to check if it is bipartite"; "BFS this component"; all solutions assign alternating colors 1 and 2
affordance_in_statement: For each tube connecting a pair of lenses, the system computes the sum of the polarization axes assigned to those two lenses. It then multiplies these sums together across all m tubes. To successfully filter out glare, this final calibration product must evaluate to exactly 3^m.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving wording change that removes this reduction: with endpoint values restricted to 1 and 2, every factor is 2, 3, or 4, so a product equal to 3^m necessarily has every factor equal to 3. Defeating it requires changing the calibration condition or adding a genuinely independent constraint.

common_affordance: Because every edge sum is one of 2, 3, or 4, a product equal to 3^m forces every edge sum to equal 3, making the task exactly bipartite two-coloring.
recommended_edit: No wording-only edit can defeat all survivors while preserving the task: the bipartite reduction is an intrinsic structural consequence. A defeating edit would have to change the product target or the allowed axis values, or add an independent constraint.
